must_fix.issue: Repeated 'fee in writing' reassurance. All five readers flagged it as filler or as sounding forced (uhnw: 'reads as reassurance for someone nervous about money'). In 05-draft-r2.md the point appears at line 10 (intro), line 17 (takeaway), line 43 (step), line 87, line 89 (question 1), line 123 (FAQ) and line 131 (close). The quoted sentence 'So on cost, you know the fee, in writing, before anything happens.' is not in r2, but the repetition is.
must_fix.fix: Say it once per role: keep the intro sentence (line 10), the step line 'The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.' (line 43, fact_23) and the close (line 131, fact_22/23/24). Cut the fee clause from takeaway line 17 or merge it into line 19. In question 1 (line 89) cut 'Ask for it in writing, before any work begins.' since line 87 already asks for answers in writing. The FAQ at line 123 is rewritten under the next must-fix and must not repeat it. Add no new cost claims.

must_fix.issue: Cost FAQ reads as a dodge (trust loss about money). Line 123 'A fee only means something next to what it covers. Ask for the fee in writing...' answers 'How much does a honeymoon planner cost?' with 'ask'. Primary persona medium objection ('As a lawyer, I notice a non-answer'), sceptic medium lost_trust, funding_parent and search_visitor ask the same.
must_fix.fix: Rewrite as a direct general answer with no figures and no claim about how Wedded Wonderland charges: say plainly there is no single price because planners charge in different ways (for example a set planning fee, a fee linked to the value of the trip, or income from supplier commissions, or a mix), so the useful comparison is what each fee covers. Then list what to ask: how the fee is worked out, what it includes, whether supplier commissions are earned on top, and when it is payable. If the writer wants to name charging models as fact, they need a source in 03-source-pack.json; otherwise frame them as questions, not statements. No ranges, no AUD figures.

should_fix.issue: Wedding-to-honeymoon handover stays general. Line 55 'The wedding week ends, the guests fly home and the two of you move on to the next stay...' is the section most about the target reader, and the primary persona wants the morning after made concrete (medium objection, top change 1).
should_fix.fix: Add one short morning-after scenario framed as planning prompts, not capability claims: what time the last guests leave, whether you need a late check-out, how luggage and wedding items get packed or sent home, the transfer to the next stay and how long it takes, and which documents travel with you. Phrase as 'things to settle before the wedding week' (for example 'Decide who is handling...'). Do not say Wedded Wonderland arranges transfers, is on the ground or has done this before (deferred).

should_fix.issue: Brochure and budget-framing phrases. 'the kind of places that make you both exhale' (line 23: sceptic turn-off, planner_couple 'slightly precious'); 'to convert at the kitchen table' (line 53: uhnw objection) and 'in what order and on what card' (line 81: uhnw turn-off, frames reader as budget-led).
should_fix.fix: Line 23: replace 'the kind of places that make you both exhale' with a plain phrase such as 'the kind of places you both want'. Line 53: end the sentence at 'two lots of quotes in foreign currencies'. Line 81: cut 'and on what card' ('how you would like to pay and in what order').

consider.issue: '### Tell us anything' heading (line 37) reads as a slogan, not a step, when scanning on a phone.
consider.fix: Rename to a plain step name, e.g. '### Step 1: Share your ideas' and, for parallel, '### Step 2: Meet your Wedded Advisor and agree the fee'. Leave the step body (fact_27 wording) unchanged. The closing CTA wording 'tell us anything' stays.

consider.issue: Duplicate FAQ. 'Who arranges the honeymoon?' (line 113) repeats 'What does a honeymoon planning service do?' (line 109).
consider.fix: Drop the 'Who arranges the honeymoon?' FAQ and its answer. Do not add a replacement question unless it is answered from the source pack.

consider.issue: Package language. Line 83 'our [honeymoon packages] show the kind of itineraries couples begin from' (uhnw medium lost_trust: 'treated like every other enquiry').
consider.fix: Soften the wording, keep the same URL: e.g. 'If it helps to see where other couples often begin, browse our [honeymoon ideas](https://weddedwonderland.com/destination-honeymoon-packages).' No claims about what the packages include.

consider.issue: No honest line on when a planner may not be needed. Sceptic medium objection at line 29 'Where a planner earns their place is time.'
consider.fix: After line 29 add one plain sentence, e.g. 'If your trip is a single stay, in one currency, with flexible dates, you may be happy booking it yourselves.' Opinion framing, no statistics.

consider.issue: Commission question (line 101) stops short. Sceptic wants the generic follow-up.
consider.fix: Extend question 7 with a reader-advice follow-up: 'If so, ask whether it is disclosed to you, and whether it affects which suppliers are recommended.' This is advice to the reader, not a statement about Wedded Wonderland.

'Make you both exhale': uhnw liked the tone, sceptic and planner_couple read it as brochure. Replace with a plain phrase; the primary persona's view and the brand rule against brochure language decide it.
